title: NEXORA options envelope key namespaces
description: The storage-key contract for the extension options envelope. This exists as data because the constraint it encodes is enforced by legacy code, not by convention: omega-pac/src/profiles.coffee:111-118 iterates only keys whose first character is '+', so any NEXORA entity stored under '+' would silently appear in availableProfiles, quick-switch lists and the generated PAC. scripts/verify.mjs reads this file and fails if any namespace violates it.

schemaVersionKey.description: The single scalar key holding the NEXORA envelope version.

profilePrefix.description: Reserved for OmegaPac profiles. NEXORA entities MUST NOT use it.

scalarPrefix.description: Every NEXORA entity lives here, one scalar key per entity, so that sync diffs and quota handling stay per-entity.

syncEligible.description: True means the value may travel through OptionsSync. It is only true for values that contain no secrets, enforced by secretBearing=false.

secretBearing.description: If true, syncEligible MUST be false and the value must be reduced to keystore references before storage. Cross-field rule checked by scripts/verify.mjs.

namespaces.description: Every NEXORA key family. scripts/verify.mjs reads this list and rejects any entry that violates the prefix, secret or schema-exists rules.

legacyOwned.description: Keys the existing engine owns. NEXORA MUST NOT redefine them; the compatibility matrix (docs/architecture/38) tracks their behaviour instead.

attachmentKeyPattern.description: Legacy RuleListProfile attachment convention (docs/audit/12). NEXORA MUST NOT reuse this prefix.

backupKeyPattern.description: Pre-migration envelope snapshot. Required and blocking before any destructive migration step (docs/architecture/35-schema-versioning-migration.md §7).

syncExcludedValueKeys.description: Value fields stripped before a profile goes to chrome.storage.sync. Two rules bound this list, and both are machine-checked because both were violated by an earlier draft of it. (1) STRIP ONLY VALUES. A `keystore://` reference is inert on another machine, so removing it buys no confidentiality -- and `userIdRef`/`headersRef`/`publicKey` are `required` in their own schemas, so stripping them makes every synced Server fail validation on the receiving machine: a REALITY server whose public key did not travel is a handshake failure the user cannot diagnose. `keystore.purge` and the receiving extension's own keystore probe are what protect a reference that arrives without its secret. (2) THE STRIP SET MUST NOT INTERSECT `required` of any sync-eligible value schema; scripts/verify.mjs asserts the intersection is empty for every namespace it registers. The legacy list is ['lastUpdate','ruleList','pacScript','sha256'] at omega-target/src/options.coffee:27 and does NOT strip 'headers', which is SEC-1; NEXORA adds 'headers', 'auth' (the per-upstream-proxy credential map read by omega-target-chromium-extension/src/module/proxy/proxy_auth.coffee:38), 'body' (raw import payload), 'gistToken' and 'token' (SEC-5's sync-backend credential, reused by WebDAV) on top of it.

secretReferences.description: The identifier and masking vocabulary for secret material, in one place. It lives in the envelope-key registry rather than in a schema of its own because every consumer of a `keystore://` string is a storage or transit key: the envelope holds references, the Connector holds values, and exactly one document has to say what a reference is allowed to look like. scripts/verify.mjs reads this block and fails if the pattern any schema property uses has drifted from `pattern`, if a concrete reference in any example or fixture violates `shape`, if a mask rule would preserve the length of a value, or if a command that writes or consumes the keystore fails to declare the errors that means.

scheme.description: The only URI scheme that denotes secret material.

pattern.description: The type-level floor, verbatim from ADR-0011 rule 2. Every schema property whose type is a keystore reference uses this string exactly -- a looser copy accepts a value, a tighter one silently splits the vocabulary in two.

shape.description: The convention every concrete reference follows: which entity owns the secret, that entity's identifier, and which field of it. The id segment is 8 to 63 characters of lowercase hex with dashes allowed, so a Server's UUID and a shorter hex prefix are both admissible -- and it is deliberately too short to be a digest of the secret, see neverDerivedFrom. scripts/verify.mjs checks `entities` and `fields` against this string and every example and fixture against the regex.

mintedBy.description: Who creates a reference, and from what.

neverDerivedFrom.description: What a reference MUST NOT be computed from. A content-addressed reference turns every synced or exported envelope into an offline dictionary against the user's credentials: the reference travels, the value does not, so anyone who guesses the value can test the guess by comparing strings.

entities.description: The owner classes that may hold a secret: `server` and `subscription` are user-visible entities, `profile` is the intent document that groups them, `sync` is a sync-backend credential, `host` is installation-scoped material the Connector mints for itself.

fields.description: The closed field vocabulary inside `shape`. A permissive tail segment is how `user`, `userId` and `user-id` ended up meaning the same thing in three files.

valueShape.description: `headers` is a map, everything else is one value. This is the only field of the vocabulary whose secret is structured, and the reason `credentials[].value` in protocol/commands/profile.import.json accepts both.

entropyClass.description: `high` means generated material whose partial display cannot rebuild it (a VLESS UUID, a feed address with a token). `low` means a human chose it, so any visible character is a clue: a passphrase's first letter and a key's length are both partial knowledge.

maxVisibleChars.description: How much of the value the UI may show for recognition, always as head-then-tail. scripts/verify.mjs forces 0 for the `low` class, so 'show the first character of the password' is not a decision a later UI can make silently.

display.description: The rules for the only places a value-shaped thing may be shown: the extension's own input fields after the user has typed it, and any structured field a masked sink emits.

lengthPreserving.description: A mask that keeps the length leaks the length, which for a passphrase policy is real information. The rendered mask is a fixed-width run of `fillChar` regardless of what is behind it.

fillChar.description: One character; the run is fixed-width, not per-character.

maskLiteral.description: What a destroyed value is replaced with in structured output (maskedConfig, a diagnostics section, an event payload) -- one fixed sentinel, so that 'this field existed and was masked' stays visible while the value does not. scripts/verify.mjs asserts the recorded fixtures use exactly this string.

appliesAt.description: Masking happens where a value leaves a process, not where a call site remembers to ask. scripts/verify.mjs does not enforce this word, docs/architecture/32 does the arguing; what it enforces is that the sink vocabulary names every exit.

fingerprint.description: The comparison primitive that lets support say 'the credential you typed is not the one on file' without either value appearing anywhere. It is the only derived representation of a secret this design permits.

pattern.description: Verbatim the shape protocol/commands/diagnostics.get.json uses for `masked.fingerprints`; scripts/verify.mjs asserts the two are the same string.

algorithm.description: Keyed, standard construction, truncated to 12 hex characters. A bare hash of a low-entropy credential is a dictionary in plain sight: the hash is deterministic, so anyone holding it can test candidates offline. No cipher of our own, per the master constraint and ADR-0011.

keyed.description: The HMAC key lives in the keystore as a `host` reference. A machine that loses its keystore cannot reproduce the fingerprints it already emitted, which is the intended behaviour: comparability is scoped to the installation, never to the world.

keyOwner.description: The reference to the fingerprint key itself.

atRest.description: What is plaintext and what is not, stated as data because the honest answer is uncomfortable: the keystore protects the envelope, not the configuration handed to Core.

blobs.description: One protected blob per secret, mechanism owned by ADR-0011 (Windows, user-scope DPAPI, no application entropy).

compiledConfigContainsValues.description: Xray reads a config file of its own format and cannot be handed references (ADR-0003). So the compiled config is, and will remain, plaintext credential material on disk -- a fact this field exists to stop anyone from later writing a document that implies otherwise.

compiledConfigOwnerOnly.description: Written in the Connector's per-user directory with inherited user-profile ACL only, never inside the extension's directory (docs/architecture/22-component-contracts.md CoreSupervisor invariant).

compiledConfigLifetime.description: When the file may be assumed to exist. It is re-derivable from intent plus keystore, so it is a cache and is deleted when it stops being needed.

compiledConfigInExports.description: No diagnostics section, log, support bundle or sync payload ever carries it; the only version of the config that leaves the Connector is `maskedConfig` (protocol/commands/config.snapshot.json).

example.description: Illustrative only; the populated registry lives in examples/envelope-keys.nexora.json so verify.mjs can check it against the schema files on disk.
